greet.speaker: host

line.py: Wǎnshang hǎo! Jǐ wèi? Yǒu dìngwèi ma?
line.en: Good evening! How many? Do you have a booking?

greet.note: A team dinner: you, two coworkers, and your manager. In this story your surname is 李 (Lǐ), and you made the booking for 7 o'clock.

text.zh: 四位，我订了七点的位子。
text.zht: 四位，我訂了七點的位子。
text.py: Sì wèi, wǒ dìng le qī diǎn de wèizi.
text.en: Four — I booked a table for seven o'clock.

choices.feedback: Both questions answered. 订位子 (dìng wèizi) = book a table.
Fine — but mention your booking (订位) so she can find it.
Numbers need a measure word in Chinese: 四位 (sì wèi) or 四个人.

surname.speaker: host

line.py: Hǎo de, qǐngwèn nín guìxìng?
line.en: Certainly — may I ask your surname?

surname.note: 贵姓 (guìxìng), "honorable surname", is the polite way to ask someone's family name.

text.py: Wǒ xìng Lǐ, mù zǐ Lǐ.
text.en: My surname is Li — the 木子 Li.

choices.feedback: Very native! People clarify a character by its parts: 李 = 木 + 子. Many surnames sound alike, so this avoids mix-ups.
Understood — but a full sentence, 我姓李, sounds friendlier.
Never use 贵 (honorable) about yourself — it's only for others. Just say 我姓李.

room.speaker: host

line.zh: 找到了。四位这边请，三号包间。
line.zht: 找到了。四位這邊請，三號包間。
line.py: Zhǎodào le. Sì wèi zhè biān qǐng, sān hào bāojiān.
line.en: Found it. This way, please — private room 3.

room.note: 包间 (bāojiān), private dining rooms, are popular for work dinners and family banquets.

seating.speaker: coworker

line.zh: 小李，你坐里面那个对着门的位子吧！
line.zht: 小李，你坐裡面那個對著門的位子吧！
line.py: Xiǎo Lǐ, nǐ zuò lǐmiàn nàge duì zhe mén de wèizi ba!
line.en: Xiao Li, take the seat at the back, facing the door!

seating.note: 小 + surname (小李) is a friendly way to address a younger colleague.

text.zh: 不不，那个位子应该请张经理坐。
text.zht: 不不，那個位子應該請張經理坐。
text.py: Bù bù, nàge wèizi yīnggāi qǐng Zhāng jīnglǐ zuò.
text.en: No, no — that seat should go to Manager Zhang.

choices.feedback: Exactly. The seat facing the door (主位, zhǔwèi) is the seat of honor for the host or the most senior person.

text.py: Wǒ zuò ménkǒu ba, fāngbiàn shàng cài.
text.en: I'll sit by the door — it's easier when the dishes come.

choices.feedback: Very humble! The seat nearest the door, where dishes are served, is the most junior seat. Your manager will be impressed.
Your coworker was testing you! The seat facing the door is the seat of honor — leave it for Manager Zhang.

line.zh: 你来点菜吧！点几个菜好？
line.zht: 你來點菜吧！點幾個菜好？
line.py: Nǐ lái diǎn cài ba! Diǎn jǐ ge cài hǎo?
line.en: You do the ordering! How many dishes should we get?

text.zh: 四个人，点四个菜一个汤吧。
text.zht: 四個人，點四個菜一個湯吧。
text.py: Sì ge rén, diǎn sì ge cài yí ge tāng ba.
text.en: There are four of us — let's get four dishes and a soup.

choices.feedback: A classic rule of thumb: one dish per person, plus a soup — all shared family-style.

text.zh: 一人一个菜，自己吃自己的。
text.zht: 一人一個菜，自己吃自己的。
text.py: Yì rén yí ge cài, zìjǐ chī zìjǐ de.
text.en: One dish each — everyone eats their own.

choices.feedback: Right number, wrong idea: Chinese meals are shared. Everyone eats from every dish.

text.py: Diǎn yí ge cài jiù gòu le.

choices.feedback: For four people? Your manager would go hungry! Try one dish per person, plus a soup.

allergy.speaker: coworker

line.py: Duì le, wǒ duì huāshēng guòmǐn.
line.en: Oh, by the way — I'm allergic to peanuts.

allergy.note: 对…过敏 (duì… guòmǐn) = "allergic to …". Several Sichuan dishes, like 宫保鸡丁, come with peanuts.

text.zh: 好，我跟服务员说不放花生。
text.zht: 好，我跟服務員說不放花生。
text.py: Hǎo, wǒ gēn fúwùyuán shuō bú fàng huāshēng.
text.en: Okay, I'll tell the server to leave out the peanuts.

choices.feedback: Good teammate! 不放 (bú fàng) = "don't put in".

text.en: Don't worry, there aren't many peanuts.

choices.feedback: Allergies are serious — even a little can be dangerous. Make sure the kitchen leaves them out.

line.zh: 几位好！这是菜单。我们的招牌菜是水煮鱼和麻婆豆腐。
line.zht: 幾位好！這是菜單。我們的招牌菜是水煮魚和麻婆豆腐。
line.py: Jǐ wèi hǎo! Zhè shì càidān. Wǒmen de zhāopái cài shì shuǐzhǔ yú hé mápó dòufu.
line.en: Hello, everyone! Here's the menu. Our signature dishes are chili-oil boiled fish and mapo tofu.

text.zh: 我同事对花生过敏，菜里都别放花生，可以吗？
text.zht: 我同事對花生過敏，菜裡都別放花生，可以嗎？
text.py: Wǒ tóngshì duì huāshēng guòmǐn, cài lǐ dōu bié fàng huāshēng, kěyǐ ma?
text.en: My coworker is allergic to peanuts — could you leave them out of everything?

choices.feedback: Clear and polite. 别放 (bié fàng) = "don't add"; 都 makes it "all of them".

text.en: What does mapo tofu taste like?

choices.feedback: Good question — listen for 麻 and 辣.
Don't forget the peanut allergy! Tell the server, or pick 不要花生 on dishes that have them.

mala.speaker: server

line.zh: 又麻又辣。“麻”是花椒的味道，舌头会麻麻的。
line.zht: 又麻又辣。「麻」是花椒的味道，舌頭會麻麻的。
line.py: Yòu má yòu là. “Má” shì huājiāo de wèidao, shétou huì mámá de.
line.en: Numbing and spicy. The "numbing" is Sichuan pepper — your tongue will tingle.

mala.note: 麻辣 (málà) = 麻 (numbing, from Sichuan peppercorns 花椒) + 辣 (hot, from chili). It's the signature flavor of Sichuan cooking.

line.py: Méi wèntí, wǒ gēn chúfáng shuō.
line.en: No problem — I'll let the kitchen know.

menu.speaker: server

line.py: Nín mànmàn kàn, diǎn hǎo le jiào wǒ.
line.en: Take your time — call me when you're ready.

menu.note: Aim for about four dishes and a soup. Rice is ordered separately.

line.zh: 问你个问题：鱼香肉丝里面有鱼吗？
line.zht: 問你個問題：魚香肉絲裡面有魚嗎？
line.py: Wèn nǐ ge wèntí: yúxiāng ròusī lǐmiàn yǒu yú ma?
line.en: Quiz time: is there any fish in "fish-fragrant" pork?

text.zh: 没有鱼！“鱼香”是一种味道，又酸又甜又辣。
text.zht: 沒有魚！「魚香」是一種味道，又酸又甜又辣。
text.py: Méiyǒu yú! “Yúxiāng” shì yì zhǒng wèidao, yòu suān yòu tián yòu là.
text.en: No fish! "Fish-fragrant" is a flavor — sour, sweet, and spicy.

choices.feedback: Correct! The sauce was originally used for cooking fish, and the name stuck.
Fair! The answer: no fish — 鱼香 is a sour-sweet-spicy sauce.
Trick question — there's no fish at all! 鱼香 is the name of the sauce.

line.py: Hǎo de, wǒ chóngfù yíxià: {order}. Duì ma?
line.en: Okay, let me repeat that: {order}. Is that right?

choices.feedback: Order placed!
Sure — back to the menu.

rice.speaker: server

line.py: Mǐfàn yào jǐ wǎn?
line.en: How many bowls of rice?

rice.note: 碗 (wǎn), "bowl", is the measure word here.

choices.feedback: One each. 四碗 — number + measure word + (noun).
For four people? Everyone usually gets their own bowl: 四碗.

text.py: Xiān bú yào mǐfàn, cài gòu le.
text.en: No rice for now — the dishes are enough.

choices.feedback: Common at banquets — rice often comes last, if at all.

toast.speaker: manager

line.py: Lái, dàjiā gānbēi!
line.en: Come on, everyone — cheers!

toast.note: 干杯 (gānbēi) literally means "dry the cup". You don't drink alcohol.

text.zh: 我不太会喝酒，以茶代酒，敬您一杯！
text.zht: 我不太會喝酒，以茶代酒，敬您一杯！
text.py: Wǒ bú tài huì hē jiǔ, yǐ chá dài jiǔ, jìng nín yì bēi!
text.en: I don't really drink — let me toast you with tea instead!

choices.feedback: 以茶代酒 (yǐ chá dài jiǔ), "tea in place of alcohol", is the graceful way to join a toast without drinking. 敬 (jìng) = to toast someone respectfully.
choices.note: When clinking glasses with someone senior, hold your glass a little lower than theirs to show respect.

text.zh: 干杯！（举起茶杯，碰得比经理低一点）
text.zht: 乾杯！（舉起茶杯，碰得比經理低一點）
text.py: Gānbēi! (Jǔ qǐ chábēi, pèng de bǐ jīnglǐ dī yìdiǎn)
text.en: Cheers! (Raise your tea and clink a little lower than the manager's glass)

choices.feedback: Perfect etiquette — a lower glass shows respect.
Honest, but blunt. Try 以茶代酒 — you still join the toast without the alcohol.

line.zh: 菜上齐了。经理还没动筷子，你可以先吃吗？
line.zht: 菜上齊了。經理還沒動筷子，你可以先吃嗎？
line.py: Cài shàng qí le. Jīnglǐ hái méi dòng kuàizi, nǐ kěyǐ xiān chī ma?
line.en: All the dishes are here. The manager hasn't picked up their chopsticks yet. Can you start eating?

choices.feedback: Inviting the most senior person to start (动筷子, dòng kuàizi) is perfect manners.
Patient and polite.
Hold on — at a formal dinner, wait for the most senior person to start first.

leftovers.speaker: server

line.zh: 吃好了吗？剩下的菜要打包吗？
line.zht: 吃好了嗎？剩下的菜要打包嗎？
line.py: Chī hǎo le ma? Shèng xià de cài yào dǎbāo ma?
line.en: All finished? Would you like the leftovers packed up?

leftovers.note: Taking leftovers home is completely normal. China even has a "clean plate" campaign against food waste (光盘行动, guāngpán xíngdòng).

text.py: Hǎo de, máfan bāng wǒmen dǎbāo.
text.en: Yes, please pack them up for us.

choices.feedback: No food wasted!

text.py: Bú yòng le, dōu chī wán le.

choices.feedback: 光盘 — clean plates!

expense.speaker: manager

line.zh: 小李，你先付，回公司报销。
line.zht: 小李，你先付，回公司報銷。
line.py: Xiǎo Lǐ, nǐ xiān fù, huí gōngsī bàoxiāo.
line.en: Xiao Li, you pay for now and claim it back at the office.

expense.note: 报销 (bàoxiāo) = to get reimbursed for an expense.

text.py: Hǎo de, wǒ huì yào fāpiào.
text.en: Sure — I'll ask for a fapiao.

choices.feedback: Smart! To claim expenses in China you need a 发票 (fāpiào), an official tax receipt.
Fine — but remember: no 发票 (official receipt), no reimbursement!

line.py: Nǐ qù jiào fúwùyuán jiézhàng.
line.en: You call the server over to pay.

choices.feedback: 帅哥 (shuàigē), "handsome guy", is an everyday friendly way to call male staff — like 美女 for women.
Classic and correct.

line.py: Yígòng {total} kuài. Xūyào fāpiào ma?
line.en: ¥{total} in total. Do you need a fapiao?

text.en: Yes, please — made out to my company.

choices.feedback: 开发票 (kāi fāpiào) = issue a fapiao; 抬头 (táitóu) is the name it's made out to. Your company will pay you back!
Oops — without a 发票 you can't claim the dinner back. This one's on you!

pay-method.speaker: server

line.py: Hǎo de. Sǎo mǎ háishi shuā kǎ?
line.en: Sure. QR code or card?

pay-method.note: 刷卡 (shuā kǎ) = to swipe a card.

choices.feedback: Done!
Done!

goodbye.speaker: host

line.py: Xièxie guānglín, gèwèi màn zǒu!
line.en: Thank you for coming — take care, everyone!

goodbye.note: 各位 (gèwèi), "everyone", is the polite way to address a group.

items.note: Despite the name ("water-boiled fish"), it arrives swimming in chili oil and Sichuan peppercorns.
Named after a pockmarked old woman (麻婆) who cooked it in 19th-century Chengdu.
Made with fried peanuts — choose 不要花生 for allergies.
Boiled, sliced, then stir-fried — "returned to the wok" (回锅).
A cold appetizer named after the couple who sold it in Chengdu. Despite 肺 (lung) in the name, it's usually beef and tripe today.
Named for the shoulder pole (担) street vendors used to carry their stoves.
A canned herbal tea people drink to "cool down" (降火) after spicy food.
